newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish finmin amends budget draft after tax vote.
newsitem.headline: Polish finmin amends budget draft after tax vote.

text.p: Poland's finance ministry on Friday amended its 1997 budget draft to take into account a personal income tax cut approved by parliament earlier this week, Finance Minister Grzegorz Kolodko said.
"I signed the budget draft amendment so that it is now compatible with parliament's tax decision," Kolodko told a news conference.

On Thursday, after a long and bitter debate, that divided the ruling leftist coaliton, parliament approved a bill lowering the three rates of the personal income tax by one point to 20, 32 and 43 percent in 1997.
The government's budget draft sent to parliament in late October was based on this year's tax rates of 21, 33 and 45 percent but Kolodko later said they could be lowered.
Kolodko confirmed his earlier statement that the cut would require increasing the 1996 budget deficit to 2.8 percent of gross domestic product from the originally planned 2.6 percent.

He also confirmed that the amendment did not change any marco-economic proportions in the draft, which provides for cutting annual inflation to 13 percent at the end of 1997 from October's 19.5 percent. @
Parliament has until January 28 to pass the budget, which will then have to be signed by President Aleksander Kwasniewski.
